data.topic: Auto-detection, self-learning, and auto-memory systems for AI coding agents — conflict detection, self-learning memory, autonomous coordination, trust calibration, auto-review loops

findings.summary: Orchestration is hierarchical planner-worker-judge: main session (Claude) plans, coders execute in worktrees, merge-worktree handles integration
findings.details: ORCHESTRATION.md defines roles: Claude (main session) calls Gemini for research, writes plan files, launches coders, merges. Coders (quick-fixer, architect) execute plans in isolated git worktrees. Main session is prohibited from using EnterWorktree. All merges go through dev branch first, then dev merges to main. This matches the hierarchical non-overlapping assignment pattern that CooperBench and Cursor found to be most effective.

findings.summary: Conflict detection is file-level with optional symbol-level granularity via pm_check_conflicts, but no AST parsing
findings.details: run-stories Step 2b calls pm_check_conflicts(story_ids=[...]) which returns write-write and write-read overlaps at file level. Symbol annotations (file.ts:functionName) allow coexistence when different functions in the same file are targeted. Conflict rules: bare file vs bare file = CONFLICT, bare vs symbol = CONFLICT, symbolA vs symbolB = SAFE. This is analogous to Grove's Tier 1-2 but without AST parsing. No dependency-level or schema-level conflict detection exists.

findings.summary: Merge is sequential within dev branch — no merge queue, stories merge one at a time via merge-worktree batch mode
findings.details: merge-worktree SKILL.md Step 3 uses git merge --no-ff into dev, with pull --rebase before each merge to prevent stale-push. Batch mode (2+ stories) delegates to a single foreground subagent that merges sequentially by story ID. No priority queue, no conflict prediction pre-merge, no automated rebase-on-conflict. README.md references a merge-queue.sh concept but the actual implementation is the batch subagent pattern.

findings.summary: Self-learning memory uses a 3-surface architecture: correction_groups (epics.db), rendered-prefs.md (sidecar), OpenMemory (semantic store)
findings.details: decision-79 killed 4 of 7 surfaces. Remaining: correction_groups table in epics.db (single source of truth for corrections), rendered-prefs.md (generated from DB at session start, survives compaction via @import), OpenMemory (queryable semantic store with per-category budgets and decay). Auto-distillation: stop hook detects corrections via semantic embedding against 10 prototype phrases (threshold 0.55), upserts to correction_groups, promotes at count >= 3. Signal processor correlates corrections with decision_preferences to adjust scores. This is a two-tier system similar to Windsurf's auto-memories + user rules, but with the RL-like signal scoring on decisions.

findings.summary: Correction detection is semantic (embedding-based) with structural pre-filters, but limited to 5 embedding calls per session and 10 static prototypes
findings.details: signal_processor.py uses CORRECTION_PROTOTYPES (10 phrases like 'stop doing that', 'why did you ignore my instruction') with cosine similarity >= 0.55 against Ollama nomic-embed-text. Pre-filters: SYSTEM_MSG regex, POSITIVE_INTENT regex, is_structural_content (>300 chars, code fences, etc.). MAX_EMBEDDING_CALLS_PER_SESSION = 5. No adaptive prototype generation — prototypes are static. decision-74 chose this over regex. The 5-call limit and static prototypes are the main bottleneck for scaling correction detection.

findings.summary: No agent health monitoring or stuck detection exists — coders run as background agents with no timeout or progress tracking
findings.details: run-stories launches coders as background agents (run_in_background: true) and waits for completion. No heartbeat, no progress check, no stuck detection. The only timeout is Claude Code's internal agent timeout. If a coder enters an infinite loop or stalls, the main session blocks indefinitely waiting for it. run-state.db tracks story_executions (pending/launched/done/blocked) but has no watchdog process checking for stalled agents. This is the gap OpenHands SDK V1 addresses with stuck detection.

findings.summary: No cross-epic parallelism — stories within an epic run in parallel, but the system assumes a single dev branch
findings.details: ORCHESTRATION.md says dev branch is always 'dev'. run-stories Step 3 ensures dev exists and all epics share it. There's no mechanism to run stories from different epics simultaneously with separate integration branches. The scope doc explicitly calls this out: 'Epic-level serialization limits throughput. Stories run in parallel but epics never do.'

findings.summary: No auto-review loop (Ralph Loop) exists — ralph-loop plugin is installed but not integrated with the orchestration pipeline
findings.details: settings.json shows 'ralph-loop@claude-plugins-official': true in enabledPlugins. The plugin exists at plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/ralph-loop/ with stop-hook.sh and setup-ralph-loop.sh. But there's no integration with run-stories or merge-worktree. No bounded iteration loops, no circuit breakers, no progress detection for autonomous code review. The overbaking phenomenon from research is a real risk if this were enabled naively.

findings.summary: All code changes must go through coder agents in worktrees — direct edits blocked by guard-direct-edit.sh
findings.details: guard-direct-edit.sh (PreToolUse hook on Edit|Write) blocks all direct edits to project source files from the main session. Coders pass because their paths resolve under .claude/worktrees/. Exceptions: ~/.claude/ behavioral files (outcomes.md, session-handoff.md, etc.), plan files, settings.json, memory files. This enforces the hierarchical architecture pattern.

findings.summary: Main session prohibited from using EnterWorktree — blocked by hook
findings.details: block-enter-worktree.sh blocks EnterWorktree tool use from the main session. Only coder subagents create/use worktrees. This is reinforced in ORCHESTRATION.md Section 1: 'MUST NOT use EnterWorktree or git worktree add'.

findings.summary: Ollama nomic-embed-text is required for all embedding operations — correction detection, OpenMemory dedup, memory queries
findings.details: embedding_utils.py calls http://localhost:11434/api/embeddings with model nomic-embed-text. All correction detection, OpenMemory writes (dedup check), and memory queries depend on it. Graceful degradation: if Ollama is down, correction detection returns empty, dedup falls back to MD5 simhash, queries return empty. load-session-context.sh checks Ollama health at session start and warns.

findings.summary: epics.db (SQLite) is the central state store — stories, epics, correction_groups, decision_preferences tables
findings.details: Located at ~/.claude/.claude/epics.db. Gemini MCP tools (pm_*) read/write stories and epics. correction_groups table stores corrections with status lifecycle (accumulating -> pending_promotion -> promoted -> dismissed). decision_preferences table stores signal scores for decision learning. run-state.db is separate for transient execution state (decision-76).

findings.summary: OpenMemory MCP provides semantic memory — openmemory.sqlite with HSG (Hierarchical Sector Graph) queries
findings.details: Registered via claude mcp add openmemory --scope user. Tools: openmemory_store, openmemory_query, openmemory_list, openmemory_get, openmemory_reinforce, openmemory_delete. Storage at ~/.claude/.claude/openmemory.sqlite. Tag taxonomy enforced by om_write.py: behavioral-pref (30), tool-learning (30), decision (50), prompt-pattern (30), session-summary (20), critique-learning (30), gemini-blind-spot (20). Anti-bloat: per-category budgets, embedding dedup (0.85), decay-weighted pruning.

findings.summary: Test infrastructure uses pytest for the Gemini MCP server — no tests for hooks, skills, or orchestration logic
findings.details: Gemini MCP server at mcp-servers/gemini/ has a .venv and pytest-based tests. The hooks (signal_processor.py, om_write.py, stop_processor.py, embedding_utils.py) have no test files. Skills are markdown-based (SKILL.md) and not unit-testable in the traditional sense. Shell scripts (worktree-setup.sh, build-verify.sh, etc.) have no test coverage. run-stories testing relies on build-verify.sh and merge-gate.py running against the actual codebase.

findings.summary: Model selection follows a tiered escalation pattern: Haiku -> Sonnet -> Opus based on failure count and complexity
findings.details: ORCHESTRATION.md Section 2: Haiku for unit-tester (never escalated), Sonnet default for coders, Opus after 2 BLOCKING round-trips (architect only). Haiku threshold requires: single write-target, exact code, no regex, no complex logic, not a pipeline file. OpenMemory queried for model+file-type failure history to pre-escalate. This is a manual trust calibration system — no automatic graduation based on success rate.

findings.summary: Stop hook runs a 5-stage background processor: corrections -> signals -> summary -> distillation -> hook generation
findings.details: session-learning-check.sh (sync fast path: mtime check) spawns stop_processor.py (nohup background). Stages: (1) correction detection via process_session_corrections, (2) signal processing correlating corrections to decisions, (3) session summary to OpenMemory, (4) auto-distillation promoting pending_promotion to promoted + om_write, (5) hook generation from newly promoted patterns. Lockfile prevents duplicate processors.

findings.summary: Outcomes logging captures story metadata for post-hoc analysis but is not used for automated decision-making
findings.details: merge-worktree Step 5.5 appends to outcomes.md: agent, model, cycle time, coder effort, skills used, friction events, tests, file count, complexity, memory attribution, what worked/failed. This is a write-only log — no code reads outcomes.md to adjust behavior automatically. The scope doc wants this to feed graduated autonomy.

decisions_relevant.summary: Correction detection uses semantic embeddings (cosine similarity 0.55 against prototypes) over regex, with Ollama nomic-embed-text
decisions_relevant.impact: Any enhancement to correction detection must stay within the embedding approach — no regex fallback. The 5-call-per-session limit and 10 static prototypes are the extension points.

decisions_relevant.summary: Correction pipeline unified into signal_processor.py process_session_corrections() — shell hooks call Python
decisions_relevant.impact: All correction detection logic must live in signal_processor.py. New detection capabilities (e.g., stuck detection, progress tracking) should extend this module, not add new detection paths.

decisions_relevant.summary: run-stories transient state in separate run-state.db — scripts own their state
decisions_relevant.impact: Agent health monitoring and progress tracking should extend run-state.db tables, not add new state stores. The schema already has story_executions and batch_verifications tables.

decisions_relevant.summary: Worktree creation moves to pre-launch via worktree-setup.sh in resolution subagent
decisions_relevant.impact: Worktree lifecycle is separated from coder logic. Any watchdog or health check must operate at the run-stories level, not inside coders.

decisions_relevant.summary: Policy-mechanism split: extract procedural blocks to scripts, keep orchestration in SKILL.md
decisions_relevant.impact: New mechanisms (merge queue, health monitor, progress tracker) should be scripts called by skills, not embedded in SKILL.md. Orchestration logic (when to invoke, how to react) stays in skills.

decisions_relevant.summary: Memory reduced to 3 persistence surfaces: correction_groups, rendered-prefs.md, OpenMemory
decisions_relevant.impact: New memory capabilities must use these 3 surfaces. Do not add new files (tool-learnings.md was killed). Extend correction_groups schema or add OpenMemory tags.

decisions_relevant.summary: Async Stop hook via nohup background subprocess — fast sync path + slow background path
decisions_relevant.impact: Post-session processing (correction detection, distillation, summary) runs asynchronously. New learning capabilities should add stages to stop_processor.py, not new hooks.

decisions_relevant.summary: Correction detection single source of truth — all detection logic in signal_processor.py
decisions_relevant.impact: No duplicating correction logic. If adding new detection methods (e.g., progress stall detection), they go in signal_processor.py.

decisions_relevant.summary: Three-tier context injection: SessionStart (always), UserPromptSubmit (on-demand), skill-specific (lazy)
decisions_relevant.impact: New context sources (e.g., agent health dashboards, trust scores) must fit the tier system. Don't load heavy context at SessionStart.

testable_assertions.verification: Read run-stories SKILL.md Step 4 — no watchdog, heartbeat, or timeout mentioned. init-run-db.py has a 1-hour stale session cleanup but no active monitoring.

testable_assertions.verification: ORCHESTRATION.md Section 1: 'dev' is the only integration branch. run-stories Step 3: pm_dev_branch returns 'dev' for all epics.

testable_assertions.assertion: Model escalation is rule-based (2 BLOCKING -> Opus) not performance-history-based
testable_assertions.verification: ORCHESTRATION.md Section 2: escalation triggered by BLOCKING count, not success rate or historical performance

testable_assertions.assertion: No automated rule deprecation or contradiction resolution exists for accumulated memories
testable_assertions.verification: om_write.py only prunes by decay-weighted score (lowest first). No semantic contradiction detection between stored memories.

conflicts.subject: Merge queue architecture
conflicts.codebase_says: Sequential merge via batch subagent with no priority queue or conflict prediction — stories merge by ID order. README.md references merge-queue.sh but actual implementation is the merge-worktree batch mode.
conflicts.research_says: Overstory implements a 4-tier FIFO merge queue with SQLite-backed state and tiered conflict resolution. Auto Claude uses three-tier conflict resolution (auto-merge, AI-powered, full-file AI merge).
conflicts.resolution: Codebase wins for initial scope. The current sequential approach is correct for single-user operation. A smart merge queue only pays off with cross-epic parallelism, which is a prerequisite change.

conflicts.subject: Conflict detection granularity
conflicts.codebase_says: File-level + optional symbol annotations via pm_check_conflicts. No AST parsing, no dependency-level analysis.
conflicts.research_says: Grove implements 5-layer detection (file, hunk, symbol, dependency, schema) with AST parsing and LRU cache. Academic work suggests semantic conflicts (clean merges with incompatible assumptions) remain unsolved.
conflicts.resolution: Codebase approach is sufficient for current scale. Adding AST parsing requires a Go/Rust binary which is out of scope. Symbol annotations already provide function-level granularity without external tooling. Dependency-level detection via pm_check_conflicts' read_conflicts is a lighter path.

conflicts.subject: Self-learning memory architecture
conflicts.codebase_says: Two-tier: auto-detected corrections (embedding-based) + manual corrections. Signal processor adjusts decision_preferences scores. 10 static prototypes, 5 calls/session.
conflicts.research_says: MemRL uses Intent-Experience-Utility triplets with RL-updated Q-values. Windsurf/Cursor auto-generate memories from interactions. MACLA learns hierarchical procedural memory via Bayesian extraction.
conflicts.resolution: Codebase already has the skeleton of MemRL's approach — signal_processor.py does score adjustment on decisions based on correction correlation (implicit RL). The gap is: (1) prototypes are static (should learn from accumulated corrections), (2) no outcome-based learning (outcomes.md is write-only), (3) no procedural memory auto-generation from successful patterns.

conflicts.subject: Agent health monitoring
conflicts.codebase_says: No active health monitoring. run-state.db cleans stale sessions >1 hour at init time. No heartbeat or stuck detection during execution.
conflicts.research_says: OpenHands SDK V1 has stuck detection (same action repeated, redundant tool calls). Overstory has tiered watchdog (mechanical daemon, AI-assisted triage, full monitor agent). Ralph-loop has circuit breakers (CB_NO_PROGRESS_THRESHOLD, CB_SAME_ERROR_THRESHOLD).
conflicts.resolution: Research wins. This is the largest gap. A lightweight progress tracker using run-state.db timestamps + a PostToolUse hook to track coder heartbeats would be a minimal viable approach. No need for Overstory's full tiered watchdog.

conflicts.subject: Trust calibration and graduated autonomy
conflicts.codebase_says: Model escalation is rule-based (2 BLOCKING -> Opus). No performance tracking, no automatic trust graduation, no success-rate-based autonomy changes.
conflicts.research_says: Anthropic data shows users organically shift to autonomous-with-intervention over ~750 sessions. No production system implements automatic performance-based graduation. Five-level framework treats autonomy as design choice.
conflicts.resolution: Opportunity to be novel. outcomes.md has the data needed for performance-based decisions (agent, model, cycle time, friction, what worked/failed). Building a simple success-rate tracker that feeds into model selection and autonomy gates would put this system ahead of any production tool.
